per_query_caveat: Same measurement caveat as inspire-poulpy: one run averaged over the example's REPEATS=10, no cross-seed spread, no separately reported client decode.
notes: The second InsPIRe construction from the paper: adds a recursive second PIR level, trading a larger query for a smaller response and less per-query work, which the authors expect to pay off on large databases. Published as its own implementation row rather than folded into inspire-poulpy — it is a different protocol and comparing it directly against single-level InsPIRe rows would be a category error. gamma0=32 with gamma1=1024; the g16 and g64 families exist in the crate and can be added as further rows if the width turns out to matter.
